issues.description: The script allows sending location data (coordinates/address) to Discord via webhook, which is a third-party server. This is a form of data exfiltration and may leak user activity or sensitive information.
issues.recommendation: Warn users and make this feature opt-in with clear consent. Do not send any user-identifiable or sensitive data without explicit permission.

issues.description: The script sends latitude and longitude to nominatim.openstreetmap.org for reverse geocoding. While this is a public API, it still transmits user location data to a third party.
issues.recommendation: Inform users about this behavior. Consider proxying requests or minimizing data sent.

issues.description: The script requests Notification API permission and can send browser notifications. This can be abused for spam or phishing if not properly controlled.
issues.recommendation: Limit notification usage and ensure it is only used for legitimate user actions.

issues.description: The script applies Proxy wrappers to native prototypes (e.g., Array.prototype.push, Element.prototype.setAttribute, Storage.prototype.setItem, String.prototype.startsWith, fetch). This can have unpredictable side effects and may break page functionality or introduce security issues if not carefully handled.
issues.recommendation: Minimize prototype pollution and avoid Proxying global prototypes unless absolutely necessary.

issues.description: The script grants GM_xmlhttpRequest but does not appear to use it for any purpose other than the two documented endpoints. No excessive permissions detected.
issues.recommendation: No action needed unless new endpoints are added.

script_name: CheatGuessr Universal | GeoGuessr | OpenGuessr | WorldGuessr | FreeGuessr
summary: This script transmits user location data (coordinates/address) to third-party servers (Discord and OpenStreetMap Nominatim) via GM_xmlhttpRequest. This is a critical privacy and data exfiltration risk. It also uses Proxy to patch native prototypes, which can introduce stability and security issues. Notification API is used, but not in a clearly abusive way. No code obfuscation or supply chain risks detected. Overall, the script poses a CRITICAL risk due to data exfiltration and privacy concerns. User consent and transparency are required. Not recommended for use in sensitive environments.
